record.paper_title: Open problems in stochastic reinforcement models
record.context_brief: Growth speed for unbounded-support reinforced sequences
record.original_question: In the reinforced sequence model with innovation probability beta and an unbounded-support base distribution mu on the positive reals, compactly supported test functions see only beta times mu in the limiting empirical measure and a proportion 1-beta of mass escapes to infinity. Since the empirical average n^{-1} sum_{i=1}^n X_i diverges, what is the superlinear rate at which sum_{i=1}^n X_i tends to infinity?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 11 Determine the speed at which (∑ n i=1 Xi) goes to infinity.
so the speed must be superlinear.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix a parameter $ eta\in(0,1)$ and a probability measure $\mu$ on $(0,\infty)$ whose support is unbounded (in particular $\int_0^\infty x\,\mu(dx)$ may be infinite). Construct a sequence $(X_n)_{n\ge 1}$ of positive random variables by the following step-reinforcement rule. Sample $X_1$ from $\mu$. For each $n\ge 1$, independently:

  - with probability $ eta$ (innovation), draw $X_{n+1}$ from $\mu$ independently of everything else;
  - with probability $1- eta$ (repetition), set $X_{n+1}=X_{U_n}$, where $U_n$ is uniformly distributed on $\{1,\dots,n\}$ independently of the past.

It is known that the empirical measure $n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n \delta_{X_i}$, tested against compactly supported continuous functions, converges weakly to $ eta\mu$, with the remaining mass $1- eta$ escaping to infinity, so that $n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n X_i	o\infty$ almost surely.

Determine the precise (necessarily superlinear) speed at which the partial sum $S_n=\sum_{i=1}^n X_i$ tends to infinity. That is, find an explicit deterministic sequence $a_n$ (depending on $ eta$ and on the tail of $\mu$) and a non-degenerate limit law (or almost-sure limit) for $S_n/a_n$ as $n	o\infty$.
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution of this growth-rate question for step-reinforced sequences with unbounded-support base distribution was located. Related literature (step-reinforced random walks, scaling exponents, Donsker-type theorems for reinforced empirical processes, reinforced Galton–Watson processes) addresses adjacent questions but not this particular superlinear-speed problem. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.snippet: Scaling exponents of step-reinforced random walks (with finite-variance / regularly varying steps).
status_evidence.claim: Existing scaling-exponent results for step-reinforced walks treat regular cases but do not resolve the unbounded-support superlinear growth question.

status_evidence.title: How linear reinforcement affects Donsker's Theorem for empirical processes
status_evidence.snippet: Glivenko–Cantelli holds for reinforced empirical measure; Donsker requires phase-dependent rescaling.
status_evidence.claim: Related results concern empirical processes, not the divergence rate of partial sums when mass escapes to infinity.
